messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: should probe affinities sum to 1?
parts:
Hi all.

Of course the log2 of whats stored in the probeaffinities.cel file, I
mean. And I mean the probe affinities summed over the probes from a
single gene.

Hopefully, it means I've simply done something wrong, or maybe I
misunderstand the PLM model. See attached.

Some of my commands below.

Thanks,
Mark

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] should probe affinities sum to 1?
parts:
When I fit the model myself using 'rlm' and compare my probe effects
with aroma's and when the probe effects sum to 0, the ones from rlm
and the ones from aroma.affymetrix are identical.

However, when the probe effects do not sum to 0, I get all kinds of
weird but systematic effects. 16 cases are in the attached PNG
file. Plotted on the y-axis is the difference between the probe
affinities.

Mark

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: should probe affinities sum to 1?
parts:
Hi Mark,

this certainly looks strange. I will have to look at this later, but
a few comments for troubleshooting.

It could have to do with the fact that you change the CDF and that
some how the ProbeAffinityFile is using the wrong/original CDF. That
would explain the "systematic effects", which I actually believe/hope
consists of the correct values but some how are offset across arrays.
For the units that give inconsistent probe affinities, could please
verify that the chip effects are consistent? That would tell us if
there is a problem with the convergence of the PLM algorithm.

Cheers

Henrik

parts:
Hi Henrik.

All looks good for the chip effects, which is what I thought.
Plotted are the squared differences (for the first 2000 transcripts)
between the chip effects from aroma and the chip effects if I pull
out the data and run the rlm myself. Note the scale on the y-axis
here ... e-14.

So, presumably the probe affinities are correct from the fit and they
get screwed up when saved to the cel file? I can help debug this if
you can suggest where to look.

Cheers,
Mark

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: should probe affinities sum to 1?
parts:
here is what i've found out so far.

1. non-zero sum probe affinities happen occasionally with ExonRmaPlm
using the standard CDF files, but with much lower frequency than the
brainarray CDFs. see attached. code below.


name<-"test_GBM"
chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType,checkChipType=F)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)

coreChipType <- paste(chipType, "core", sep=",")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(coreChipType)

setCdf(cs, cdf)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,mergeGroups=T)

fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
ces<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
pes<-getProbeAffinities(plm)

x<-readUnits(csN,units=1:22010)
y<-readUnits(ces,units=1:22010)
z<-readUnits(pes,units=1:22010)

> pas<-rep(NA,length(z))
> for(i in 1:length(pas)) pas[i]<-sum(log2(z[[i]][[1]]$phi))
> plot(pas,pch=".")

> sum(abs(pas))>.1
[1] TRUE
> sum(abs(pas)>.1)
[1] 51

will try some more debugging tomorrow.

cheers,
mark

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: should probe affinities sum to 1?
parts:
Hi folks.

A bit stumped here.

If I fit the PLM on the whole set of units (I've picked
units=20790:56283 here since the brainarray CDF has 20789 single
probe units which I think are control probes?), and I pull out the
probe effects for the 5th one (z[[5]] below), it gives me probe
effects which sum to -5.009. If I pull out the data (yy below), and
call 'fitUnit' for this object and use 'updateUnits' to write it to
the probeAffinities.cel file, it gets a set of probe affinities that
basically sum to 0 (some roundoff). The chip effects are basically
unchanged either way, so there is no problem with the fits themselves.

I have played a bit with 'updateUnits' but haven't figured out why it
writes something differently when you call on all units compared with
a single unit. Could be something in 'readUnits' too, I dunno.

Still looking, but if anyone has any suggestions, I'm all ears.

Mark

> pes<-getProbeAffinities(plm)

> x<-readUnits(csN,units=20790:56283)

> z<-readUnits(pes,units=20790:56283)

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: should probe affinities sum to 1?
parts:
Hi all.

Well, the answer is simple. Sadly, it took me my whole day to figure
it out.

Basically, with the brainarray annotation, you can have a probe that
is part of several probesets. Problem is, you may get a different
estimated probe affinity for a particular probe in the different
transcripts and when you try and write them to a file all at the
same, the indices clash (because you can only store 1 probe affinity
per probe!) and only one gets stored.

This explains why when I write the whole set of probe affinities to
file at one time, this problem occurs, but when I 'updateUnits' on a
single probeset, I read out the correct result. Its so obvious
(well, it is now). This also explains why the chip effects are
unaffected.

If you have non-overlapping probesets, there will be no problems,
which is why the 'core' human exon CDF that Ken created has no problems.

So, I will have to resort to an alternative approach than reading
from the probe affinity files for my application.

Mark

> the probeAffinities.cel file, it gets a set of probe affinities that
> basically sum to 0 (some roundoff). The chip effects are basically

that was tricky, but it all make sense when you explain it. I did not
know about this many-to-one mapping.

CDF? Btw, is that the name of the chip type? Do you know if apples
to any of the other two exon arrays in Section "Documentation on chip
types";

type, and 2) add some warning text reminding us of the problem.

CEL files requires a one-to-one mapping.

problem?
